instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor. Analyse the company profile and survey responses, then respond ONLY with a valid JSON object containing maturity_score, opportunities, next_steps, and key_weaknesses.

answers.companyDescription: Corporate finance advisory boutique specializing in M&A, capital raising, and valuation services for technology and healthcare companies in the €5M-€100M deal range. The firm operates with deep industry relationships and focuses on complex structuring and exit strategies within high-growth sectors. They have successfully closed 28 significant transactions over the past two years.
answers.pastInitiatives: We launched a digital customer onboarding flow last quarter that reduced average onboarding time from 12 days to 5 days. The project was cross-functional involving product, compliance, and customer success teams. Early NPS scores for new customers onboarded through this flow are 22 points higher than the legacy process, validating our approach to efficiency.
answers.strategicGoals: Our board has set an ambitious revenue target of reaching €50M ARR within 5 years from our current base. This requires us to expand our addressable market, potentially pivot pricing models from one-time to recurring revenue, and build a repeatable enterprise sales motion. We need to identify the highest-leverage growth levers without overextending our cash runway.
answers.teamSize: The innovation function is informal – one senior engineer has been given permission to spend 20% of their time exploring new technologies and prototyping ideas, but this allocation is frequently interrupted by production incidents and urgent feature requests. We have no dedicated innovation budget beyond standard cloud infrastructure costs.
answers.additionalContext: The firm maintains strong ties with key industry influencers, which provides early insights into M&A trends that competitors miss. Internal discussions are currently focused on leveraging proprietary data sets to create a predictive valuation model.

opportunities.title: AI-Assisted Deal Structuring Tool Refinement
opportunities.rationale: Leveraging the existing interest in an AI-assisted tool can incrementally improve efficiency and service quality for M&A due diligence. This addresses internal knowledge bottlenecks while keeping the risk manageable.

first_actions: Allocate 10% of the senior engineer's time specifically to prompt engineering and data integration testing.
Define clear, measurable performance metrics for the tool (e.g., reduction in due diligence hours by 20%).
Test the AI model against 5 recent transaction datasets.
resources_needed: Subscription costs for specialized financial data APIs (€3k/quarter)
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in average deal valuation analysis time by 15%.
milestones: Q1: Tool validation and initial workflow integration.
Q2: Pilot deployment with two live advisory projects.

opportunities.title: Recurring Advisory SaaS Platform Development (Growth Lever)
opportunities.rationale: Pivoting from a pure transaction model to a subscription service for ongoing capital raising strategy or market intelligence provides a high-leverage growth path. This aligns with the strategic goal of recurring revenue.

first_actions: Conduct market research on niche, recurring advisory needs in healthcare tech (e.g., VC funding support).
Establish an MVP for a 'Strategic Readiness Dashboard' to be offered as a subscription tier.
Secure small seed funding specifically earmarked for R&D (€50k total).
resources_needed: Hiring support for fractional sales/product development.
execution_plan.success_metric: Achieve 10 paying subscription clients within 9 months.
milestones: Q3: MVP launch and initial beta testing with pilot clients.
Q4: Full revenue stream validation of the recurring model.

next_steps.action: Formalize an Innovation Steering Committee and assign clear ownership for the radical SaaS concept.
Conduct a detailed feasibility study on recurring revenue models versus pure transactional growth levers.

key_weaknesses: Owner-alone decision making severely limits speed and scope of experimentation.
Informal innovation function leads to difficulty in scaling experimental successes or managing technical debt.
Limited dedicated budget (17%) restricts long-term radical investment and talent acquisition needed for growth.
High dependency on specific senior personnel, creating a single point of failure risk.
